entries.reviewSummary: Provides reporting requirements, program exit rules, state profit sharing, sunset provisions, and rulemaking for rural investment funds.

headings.title: Citation of Regulatory Sandbox Act
headings.reviewNote: Designates sections 620.3900 to 620.3930 as the Regulatory Sandbox Act.

headings.title: Definitions for regulatory sandbox program
headings.reviewNote: Defines advisory committee, applicable agency, consumer, innovative offering, regulatory relief office, and related statutory terms.

entries.reviewSummary: Enacts the Regulatory Sandbox Act and defines core statutory terms for the regulatory sandbox program.

headings.title: Creation of regulatory relief office
headings.reviewNote: Creates the regulatory relief office within the department to be administered by a sandbox program director.

headings.title: Duties of regulatory relief office
headings.reviewNote: Outlines office duties to administer the program, act as liaison, evaluate applications, and coordinate with state agencies.

headings.title: Review of burdensome laws and regulations
headings.reviewNote: Directs the office to review burdensome laws, create a consumer/environmental risk framework, pursue governor-ordered reciprocity agreements with advisory committee support, adopt federal/state best practices, consult businesses, and promulgate chapter 536 rules (August 28, 2024).

headings.title: Public regulatory suggestion webpage and quarterly reports
headings.reviewNote: Requires a department webpage inviting residents and businesses to suggest laws and regulations for modification or elimination, and directs quarterly written reports to the governor and general assembly protecting nonpublic commenters.

headings.title: Annual report to governor and legislature
headings.reviewNote: Requires annual reports by October first detailing sandbox participants, economic impact, and recommended permanent rule changes.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Regulatory Relief Office, defining administrative duties, regulatory review functions, public reporting, and annual reports.

headings.title: Establishment of sandbox advisory committee
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the general regulatory sandbox program advisory committee to evaluate applications and advise the office.

headings.title: Terms of office and appointing authorities
headings.reviewNote: Sets four-year terms for committee members appointed by the governor and legislative leaders.

headings.title: Quorum and official actions of committee
headings.reviewNote: Provides that a majority constitutes a quorum and actions require an affirmative vote of the majority.

headings.title: Authority to override regulatory office decisions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the advisory committee to override decisions of the regulatory relief office by a two-thirds majority vote.

headings.title: Advisory duties regarding sandbox applications
headings.reviewNote: Directs the committee to review applications and make recommendations regarding waiver or suspension of state regulations.

headings.title: Staff support provided by relief office
headings.reviewNote: Directs the regulatory relief office to provide administrative and staff support for the advisory committee.

headings.title: Expense reimbursement without compensation
headings.reviewNote: Provides that committee members serve without compensation but may be reimbursed for actual and necessary expenses.

headings.title: Public meetings subject to sunshine law
headings.reviewNote: Requires committee meetings to be open public meetings subject to chapter 610 with closed records exceptions.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the General Regulatory Sandbox Program Advisory Committee, detailing membership, veto authority, meetings, and duties.

headings.title: Application requirements for sandbox program
headings.reviewNote: Sets forth required information in applications to participate in the regulatory sandbox program.

headings.title: Application fee of three hundred dollars
headings.reviewNote: Requires applicants to remit a three-hundred-dollar application fee per innovative offering to be used by the regulatory relief office solely to implement sections 620.3900 to 620.3930.

headings.title: Separate application for each innovative offering
headings.reviewNote: Requires applicants to submit distinct applications for each separate innovative offering sought to be demonstrated.

headings.title: Preapplication consultation with relief office
headings.reviewNote: Permits prospective applicants to request informal consultations with the office prior to formal filing.

headings.title: Agency consultation and review timeline
headings.reviewNote: Directs the office to consult with applicable state agencies within sixty days of application filing.

headings.title: Agency objection and consumer protection standards
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes agencies to object to waivers if consumer harm, safety risks, or financial instability would result.

headings.title: Transmission of applications to advisory committee
headings.reviewNote: Requires the director to provide applications and agency reports to the advisory committee for review.

headings.title: Consultation before approving sandbox application
headings.reviewNote: Requires consultation with applicable agencies and the advisory committee before final application approval.

headings.title: Evaluation factors for innovative offerings
headings.reviewNote: Specifies statutory factors considered when reviewing applications, including consumer benefit and safety.

headings.title: Written agreement required for participation
headings.reviewNote: Requires approved applicants to execute a written agreement detailing terms, conditions, and waived regulations.

headings.title: Discretionary denial and mandatory disqualifications
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes director denial and mandates disqualification for applicants convicted of theft or fraud crimes.

headings.title: Website publication of approved participants
headings.reviewNote: Requires public notice of approved sandbox participants on the department website upon agreement execution.

headings.title: Public records and trade secret protection
headings.reviewNote: Treats applications as public records under chapter 610 while exempting proprietary business trade secrets.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs regulatory sandbox application procedures, fees, agency reviews, evaluation criteria, agreements, and public disclosure.

headings.title: Twenty-four month demonstration period authorized
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes sandbox participants to demonstrate innovative offerings for twenty-four months following approval.

headings.title: Consumer residency and restitution protections
headings.reviewNote: Restricts offerings to consumers and prohibits waiving regulations if doing so prevents restitution for harm.

headings.title: Out-of-state licensure and regulatory standing
headings.reviewNote: Preserves participant rights to act in other jurisdictions under valid out-of-state licenses or authorizations.

headings.title: Enforcement suspension during demonstration period
headings.reviewNote: Bars prosecution and administrative penalties for regulatory violations waived in the written agreement.

headings.title: Exclusion of criminal offenses from immunity
headings.reviewNote: Explicitly provides that sandbox participants retain no immunity from criminal offenses committed during the demonstration.

headings.title: Termination of participation by relief office
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the office to terminate participation at any time, subject to a two-thirds override vote by the committee.

headings.title: Immunity from liability for program decisions
headings.reviewNote: Grants immunity from civil liability to the office and employees for application denials or program terminations.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs the demonstration period, regulatory enforcement suspensions, consumer protections, terminations, and state liability immunities.

headings.title: Mandatory consumer disclosure statements
headings.reviewNote: Requires sandbox participants to disclose participant contact information, program status, waived regulations, risks, and complaint mechanisms.

headings.title: Clear and conspicuous disclosure delivery
headings.reviewNote: Mandates that disclosures be provided clearly and conspicuously with required electronic acknowledgment before transactions.

headings.title: Authority to require additional disclosures
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the regulatory relief office to mandate additional consumer disclosures tailored to specific innovative offerings.

entries.reviewSummary: Specifies required consumer disclosures, acknowledgment procedures, and additional disclosure authority under the regulatory sandbox.

headings.title: Notice of program exit or extension
headings.reviewNote: Requires sandbox participants to notify the office of intent to exit or seek an extension forty-five days before demonstration ends.

headings.title: Automatic expiration of demonstration period
headings.reviewNote: Provides that demonstration periods automatically end after twenty-four months if no timely notice or extension request is filed.

headings.title: Ongoing services subject to normal regulations
headings.reviewNote: Subjects ongoing services continued after the demonstration period to full regulatory enforcement.

headings.title: Extension request and review procedure
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes twelve-month demonstration extensions upon application review and consultation with applicable state agencies.

headings.title: Twenty-four-month record retention and office inspection
headings.reviewNote: Requires participants to retain business records for twenty-four months after exit and make them available upon office request, with noncompliance resulting in program removal.

headings.title: Notice and consumer protection upon early cessation
headings.reviewNote: Requires a participant ceasing an innovative offering before the end of the demonstration period to notify the office and each applicable agency and report consumer protection actions taken.

headings.title: Quarterly participant reporting requirements
headings.reviewNote: Directs the regulatory relief office to establish quarterly reporting requirements for each sandbox participant, including information on consumer complaints.

headings.title: Thirty-day post-exit report and public posting
headings.reviewNote: Requires a written overview report within thirty days of exit detailing consumer harm, legal actions, and agency complaints (barring noncompliant participants and leadership from future participation), with non-trade-secret incidents posted publicly.

headings.title: Applicable agency written reform report
headings.reviewNote: Requires each applicable agency, within thirty days of receiving a quarterly or post-exit report, to submit a written report to the office recommending statutory or regulatory reforms.

headings.title: Participant removal for unwaived violations
headings.reviewNote: Permits the regulatory relief office to remove a participant at any time for violating sections 620.3900 to 620.3930 or unwaived laws or regulations, with non-trade-secret removal information posted publicly.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs regulatory sandbox exit notices, automatic expiration, extensions up to seven years, record retention, early cessation notices, quarterly and post-exit reports, agency reform reports, and participant removal.

headings.title: Establishment of Missouri Ireland trade commission
headings.reviewNote: Creates the nine-member Missouri Ireland Trade Commission within the department, comprising three senators, three representatives, and three governor-appointed, senate-confirmed public members.

headings.title: Statutory study duties and bilateral trade
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission to study bilateral trade, investment, business partnerships, cultural ties, and educational exchanges.

headings.title: Appointment deadline, member terms, and vacancies
headings.reviewNote: Requires appointments within ninety days after August 28, 2026, sets two-year legislative terms and four-year gubernatorial terms, and directs filling vacancies in the original manner.

headings.title: Expense reimbursement without compensation
headings.reviewNote: Provides that commission members serve without compensation but may be reimbursed for actual expenses.

headings.title: Meetings, hearings, and quorum requirements
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission to meet, hold statewide hearings, elect officers, and defines quorum standards.

headings.title: Annual report to governor and legislature
headings.reviewNote: Requires the commission to submit an annual report of findings and recommendations to the governor and general assembly.

headings.title: Fundraising and Ireland trade commission fund
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes private fundraising and creates the Missouri Ireland Trade Commission Fund in the state treasury.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Missouri Ireland Trade Commission, specifying membership, bilateral trade study duties, meetings, reporting, and fundraising.

headings.title: Recognition of historic legacy trails
headings.reviewNote: Statutorily recognizes specified historical trails as the Historic Legacy Trails of Missouri.

headings.title: Signage review and department coordination
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to verify trail signage, coordinate with state agencies, and place signs subject to appropriation.

entries.reviewSummary: Recognizes Missouri Historic Legacy Trails and provides for state signage review and installation.

headings.title: Establishment of Rock Island trail community designation
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the municipal designation of Missouri Rock Island Trail Community.

headings.title: Statutorily designated trail municipalities
headings.reviewNote: Lists specific municipalities along the Rock Island Trail designated as trail communities.

headings.title: Procedure for designating additional municipalities
headings.reviewNote: Provides that additional municipalities along the Rock Island Trail corridor may be designated as Missouri Rock Island Trail communities by act of the general assembly.

headings.title: Expenditure of state funds not required
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that nothing in the section requires the expenditure of state funds.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Missouri Rock Island Trail Community designation, enumerates qualifying municipalities, and provides for future designations.

headings.title: Director of tourism qualifications and compensation
headings.reviewNote: Requires commission employment of a qualified director of tourism and sets compensation limits.

headings.title: Employment of professional staff by director
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the director of tourism to employ professional and clerical staff with commission consent.

headings.title: State merit system coverage for staff
headings.reviewNote: Directs that all staff members except the director shall be employed under the state merit system.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs appointment of the director of tourism, staff employment, compensation, and state merit system coverage.

headings.title: Definitions for tourism marketing
headings.reviewNote: Defines director, fund, marketing, person, promotion, special item, and trademark for tourism marketing operations.

headings.title: Establishment of tourism marketing fund
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Tourism Marketing Fund exempt from section 33.080 biennial lapse unless the balance exceeds one and one-half times prior-year appropriation expenditures, with investment earnings credited to the fund.

headings.title: Authority to market promotional items and logos
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to market special items, register state logos, and license promotional materials.

headings.title: Written consent and royalties for special items
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits unauthorized marketing of special items and authorizes the director to require royalty payments.

headings.title: State tax exemption for promotional marketing
headings.reviewNote: Exempts the director, state agencies, and commissions from state taxes on special item marketing.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Tourism Marketing Fund, authorizes official promotional merchandise licensing, requires royalties, and provides tax exemptions.

headings.title: Creation of tourism supplemental revenue fund
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Division of Tourism Supplemental Revenue Fund in the state treasury consisting of appropriations and federal, private, or other gifts, grants, and bequests, exempt from section 33.080 biennial lapse.

headings.title: Submission of annual marketing strategy
headings.reviewNote: Requires the division of tourism to submit a comprehensive promotional marketing strategy before fund appropriations are made.

entries.reviewSummary: Creates the Division of Tourism Supplemental Revenue Fund and requires submission of an annual marketing strategy prior to appropriations.

headings.title: Citation of Small Business Incubators Act
headings.reviewNote: Designates the statutory section as the Small Business Incubators Act.

headings.title: Definitions for business incubator program
headings.reviewNote: Defines department, incubator, local sponsor, participant, and related statutory terms.

headings.title: Establishment of incubator loan and grant program
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a loan, loan guarantee, and grant program to support small business incubator creation.

headings.title: Application review and acceptance criteria
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to review and accept applications based on local sponsor ability, community economic impact, conformance with local and areawide development plans, and statewide geographic distribution.

headings.title: Administration of loans and matching requirements
headings.reviewNote: Restricts loans, loan guarantees, and grants to listed facility and business development costs, caps assistance at fifty percent of eligible project costs, and permits discretionary deferral of interest and principal.

headings.title: Duties and responsibilities of local sponsor
headings.reviewNote: Outlines local sponsor responsibilities including facility management, leases, and tenant business assistance.

headings.title: Department rulemaking, awards, compliance, and annual reports
headings.reviewNote: Permits department rulemaking and awards of loans, loan guarantees, and grants, and requires ensuring sponsor compliance and evaluating local sponsor annual reports.

headings.title: Review and conversion of previous loans to grants
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to review previous incubator loans and convert them to grant status where appropriate in the department's judgment.

headings.title: Annual reporting by department to legislature
headings.reviewNote: Requires annual reports to the governor and legislature evaluating incubator program outcomes and job creation.

headings.title: Establishment of incubator fund in treasury
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Missouri small business incubator fund in the state treasury to hold repayments, fees, and appropriations.

headings.title: Tax credit for contributions to incubators
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a fifty percent state tax credit for taxpayers making contributions to approved incubator sponsors.

headings.title: Transfer and assignment of incubator tax credits
headings.reviewNote: Permits taxpayers to sell, assign, or convey incubator tax credits and sets endorsement procedures.

entries.reviewSummary: Enacts the Small Business Incubators Act, establishing loan and grant programs, fund operations, reporting, contribution credits, and transfers.

headings.title: Establishment of small business assistance office
headings.reviewNote: Creates the small business assistance office within the department to operate regional one-stop guidance centers.

headings.title: Duties of regional business assistance offices
headings.reviewNote: Outlines office duties to counsel businesses, simplify regulations, coordinate permits, and facilitate procurement.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Small Business Assistance Office and regional one-stop guidance centers, specifying statutory duties to assist entrepreneurs.

headings.title: Higher education contracts for business assistance
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to contract with institutions of higher education to operate business assistance offices.

headings.title: Research, development, and feasibility studies
headings.reviewNote: Permits business assistance offices to provide research, training, needs assessments, and market feasibility studies.

headings.title: Performance appraisal measures and contract criteria
headings.reviewNote: Requires quantifiable performance measures and marketing goals as criteria for awarding or renewing office contracts.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes higher education contracts for business assistance offices, specifying study functions and performance appraisal criteria.

headings.title: Purpose of Show-Me heroes program
headings.reviewNote: Establishes program purpose to assist spouses of deployed military personnel and help returning service members find employment.

headings.title: Participant eligibility and supportive services
headings.reviewNote: Outlines participant hardship criteria and authorizes job training, child care, and family support services.

headings.title: Grants to nonprofits for veteran apprenticeship programs
headings.reviewNote: Permits the department of higher education and workforce development to award grants to nonprofit organizations to recruit or assist veterans and transitioning active-duty personnel in USDOL-certified apprenticeship training programs.

headings.title: Department administrative rulemaking authority
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to promulgate implementing rules under chapter 536 with nonseverability clauses for rules proposed or adopted after August 28, 2012.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Show-Me Heroes program to assist deployed military families and returning service members with supportive services and nonprofit veteran apprenticeship grants.

headings.title: Three corps programs for youth and young adults
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Missouri youth service and conservation corps consisting of a year-round community services and conservation program, a summer employment program, and a youth volunteer program.

headings.title: Priority eligibility for disadvantaged youths
headings.reviewNote: Directs priority enrollment for economically disadvantaged, at-risk, and unemployed youth.

headings.title: Geographic eligibility, felony bar, and unemployment requirement
headings.reviewNote: Makes urban and rural residents eligible to apply, bars persons convicted of a felony within the previous two years, and requires participants to be unemployed at enrollment.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the three Missouri Youth Service and Conservation Corps programs, prioritizes dropouts and at-risk youth, and sets urban/rural residency, felony, and unemployment eligibility rules.

headings.title: Community services and conservation program projects
headings.reviewNote: Defines the program as projects offering young adults paid work experience integrated with educational activities such as employability skills training and educational remediation.

headings.title: GED, remediation, approved wages, and job-search time
headings.reviewNote: Requires dropouts to pursue a GED and at-risk youth to attend remediation classes under approved work schedules, mandates division-approved wages, and permits eight hours weekly of paid job-search time during the final three weeks.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes paid work experience and educational remediation for the community services and conservation program, including GED completion, wages, and job-search leave.

headings.title: Summer employment program projects and eligibility
headings.reviewNote: Defines the summer employment program as paid work experience integrated with educational activities and requires participants to be unemployed at enrollment.

headings.title: Remediation and basic skills training
headings.reviewNote: Requires integration of academic remediation and work readiness training into summer employment.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes summer youth employment programs and mandates basic skills remediation.

headings.title: Department administration and program rules
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to administer youth service programs and adopt administrative regulations.

headings.title: Interagency cooperation and chapter 34 contracting exemption
headings.reviewNote: Requires division cooperation and permits direct contracting with state agencies, local governments, advisory councils, and nonprofits without being governed by chapter 34.

headings.title: Funding assistance contracts, application contents, and match
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes funding assistance contracts with Workforce Investment Act entities and project sponsors based on applications detailing project goals, corps members, budgets, requested assistance, and at least twenty-five percent sponsor financial support.

headings.title: Private industry council review and local signatures
headings.reviewNote: Requires applications to be reviewed by the local private industry council and signed by the workforce investment board chairperson and chief local elected official before submission.

headings.title: Notice and comment for affected state agencies
headings.reviewNote: Directs the division to notify all affected state agencies of applications and allow comments on project feasibility and other available funding.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes division administration and direct contracting exempt from chapter 34, sets application contents and twenty-five percent sponsor match, and requires local workforce signatures and state agency comment.

headings.title: Minimum wage and statutory benefit exemptions
headings.reviewNote: Requires paying participants at least minimum wage (except youth volunteers), exempts corps workers from merit systems and public retirement, and excludes qualifying work-relief or work-training services from chapter 288 employment.

headings.title: Administrative expense limitations
headings.reviewNote: Caps project sponsor administrative expenditures at ten percent of total grant funding.

headings.title: Prohibition on replacing workers or impairing contracts
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits awarding funds to any program that replaces or supplants workers in an authorized work stoppage or currently employed workers, or impairs existing service contracts.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes project sponsor wage and benefit standards, caps administrative expenses at ten percent, and prohibits replacing striking or existing workers.

headings.title: Annual evaluation of program effectiveness
headings.reviewNote: Directs the Missouri training and employment council to review and recommend evaluation criteria, program criteria, and priorities for division monitoring of youth corps projects.

headings.title: Academic credit, tuition grants, and loan incentives
headings.reviewNote: Directs the division to work with higher education, elementary and secondary education, colleges, and lenders to develop academic credit, tuition grants, and deferred loan repayment incentives and adopt chapter 536 rules.

headings.title: Recognition of Show-Me employers
headings.reviewNote: Directs the division of workforce development to establish and promote Show-Me Employers consisting of Missouri businesses agreeing to interview youth corps graduates for entry-level jobs.

headings.title: Promotion of corps within labor exchange system
headings.reviewNote: Directs the division of workforce development to recognize and promote the youth service corps and the benefits of hiring its graduates within the labor exchange system.

entries.reviewSummary: Directs council evaluation criteria, interagency academic and tuition incentives, Show-Me Employer recruitment, and labor exchange promotion for youth corps graduates.

headings.title: Citation of Missouri Innovation, Public Safety, and Accountability Act
headings.reviewNote: Designates sections 620.6000 to 620.6033 as the Missouri Innovation, Public Safety, and Accountability Act.

headings.title: Definitions for innovation zone act
headings.reviewNote: Defines twenty statutory terms including application, baseline, city, department, executive branch, main street district, master plan, master scorecard, Missouri innovation zone, net-new local, property, and state revenues, new job, participating city, reviewing authority, state baseline year, and tax increments.

entries.reviewSummary: Enacts the Missouri Innovation, Public Safety, and Accountability Act and defines core statutory terms for Missouri innovation zone programs.

headings.title: Establishment of statewide innovation zone program
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the statewide Missouri innovation zone program to provide economic development incentives to eligible cities.

headings.title: Limitation to one zone per city
headings.reviewNote: Limits each city to one certified Missouri innovation zone, defines geographic boundaries, makes participation voluntary, and requires no local legislative act, ordinance, or resolution for designation or certification.

headings.title: Master plan application requirements for cities
headings.reviewNote: Requires the city executive branch to submit a master plan detailing boundaries, vacant or under-utilized properties, public safety and infrastructure priorities, reinvestment strategy, and projections, and to oversee post-certification implementation.

headings.title: Department review and certification timeline
headings.reviewNote: Directs forty-five-day review of complete master plans, fifteen-day deficiency cure with thirty-day resumed review, conditional designation pending section 620.6006 local policies, and certification by operation of law upon department inaction.

headings.title: Available incentives upon zone certification
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes state and local incentives upon zone certification, subject to master scorecard evaluations and rules.

headings.title: Administration of statutory economic incentives
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that each statutory incentive shall be administered by the designated agency or local governing authority.

headings.title: Administration of rural development fund
headings.reviewNote: Designates the department as administrator of the rural Missouri development fund pursuant to section 620.6009.

headings.title: Administration of public safety fund
headings.reviewNote: Directs the participating city executive branch to administer the public safety fund under section 620.6012.

headings.title: Department of revenue administration of opportunity zones
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the Missouri opportunity zone incentive under section 620.6027 shall be administered by the department of revenue through tax filing, certification, and reporting procedures.

headings.title: Administration of retention and relocation incentives
headings.reviewNote: Directs department administration of retention, reinvestment, and relocation incentives under sections 620.6018 and 620.6021.

headings.title: Scoring of office conversion incentives
headings.reviewNote: Requires office-to-residential conversion incentives to be reviewed, scored via master scorecard, and administered by the department.

headings.title: Administration of angel investment incentives
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to administer angel investment incentives pursuant to sections 620.6030 and 620.6033.

headings.title: Local tax abatement and financing administration
headings.reviewNote: Provides that local tax abatement and tax increment financing shall be administered by local authorities under section 620.6006.

headings.title: Adoption and standards of master scorecard
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to promulgate rules establishing the master scorecard to objectively evaluate proposed incentive projects.

headings.title: Applicant burden of proof for scorecard
headings.reviewNote: Places the burden on applicants to demonstrate compliance with master scorecard criteria and submit required certifications.

headings.title: Authority for additional locally administered incentives
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that participating cities may award additional local incentives consistent with state law regardless of scorecard score.

headings.title: Protection of existing city revenues
headings.reviewNote: Provides that incentives shall apply solely to net-new assessed value without abating or impairing existing city revenues.

headings.title: General legal compliance as eligibility condition
headings.reviewNote: Maintains full compliance with criminal, tax, labor, and reporting laws as an independent eligibility condition.

headings.title: State-administered application review and deemed approval
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a forty-five-day department determination timeline with deemed approval provisions for complete state applications.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Missouri Innovation Zone Program, defining zone certification, master scorecard criteria, incentive administration, and review timelines.

headings.title: Condition of certification and participation
headings.reviewNote: Requires participating cities to establish and maintain specified municipal policies within innovation zone boundaries.

headings.title: Definitions for municipal innovation zone policies
headings.reviewNote: Defines application, complete application, locally administered development initiative, one stop review authority, and submission.

headings.title: Establishment of municipal one-stop shop
headings.reviewNote: Mandates that each participating city establish and maintain a coordinated one-stop shop review process.

headings.title: Scope of municipal one-stop shop review
headings.reviewNote: Applies one-stop shop review to development applications, local incentives, and business license approvals.

headings.title: Preservation of state-administered incentive procedures
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that the section does not alter separate statutory procedures for state-administered economic incentives.

headings.title: Electronic application submission requirement
headings.reviewNote: Requires participating cities to provide an online filing system generating automatic dated receipts for submissions.

headings.title: Website publication of application checklists
headings.reviewNote: Directs participating cities to publish standardized checklists on their websites for development, business, and master-scorecard local incentive applications, barring incompleteness findings for unlisted materials.

headings.title: Preapplication conference process for major projects
headings.reviewNote: Directs the one stop review authority to offer a preapplication conference for major projects meeting subsection 9(14) thresholds or designated by ordinance, without making participation mandatory unless required by prior ordinance.

headings.title: One stop review authority responsibilities
headings.reviewNote: Outlines duties of the review authority to verify completeness, track deadlines, and coordinate municipal department sign-offs.

headings.title: Cost-recovery limitations on municipal development fees
headings.reviewNote: Requires participating cities to limit permit, plan review, inspection, and development fees in certified zones to actual, reasonable, direct costs rather than percentage-of-value or construction-cost metrics.

headings.title: Existing agreements, non-TIF property increment, and elections
headings.reviewNote: Preserves existing TIF and abatement agreements, directs fifty percent of net-new local property tax revenue from non-TIF properties into the innovation zone public safety fund, and allows new projects to elect TIF, abatement, or neither.

headings.title: Building code flexibility for adaptive reuse
headings.reviewNote: Directs participating cities to provide building code flexibility for historic structures and adaptive reuse projects.

headings.title: City noncompliance remediation and decertification
headings.reviewNote: Requires written notice of noncompliance with a forty-five-calendar-day cure period before prospective suspension of zone certification, without impairing prior approved incentives or agreements.

headings.title: Biennial department report to legislature
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to submit biennial reports to the general assembly on zone performance and economic metrics.

headings.title: Department retention of administrative revenues
headings.reviewNote: Permits the department to retain an appropriated portion of net-new state revenues to fund administrative oversight.

headings.title: Severability of innovation zone provisions
headings.reviewNote: Establishes severability for sections 620.6000 to 620.6033 if any provision or application is held invalid.

headings.title: Information sharing between state departments
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department of revenue to disclose confidential state tax information to the department, state treasurer, and administering agencies or local governments as necessary to verify, administer, or enforce sections 620.6000 to 620.6033.

headings.title: Department administrative rulemaking authority
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to promulgate necessary rules under chapter 536 with nonseverability provisions affecting rules proposed or adopted after August 28, 2026.

headings.title: Sunset and termination under sunset act
headings.reviewNote: Specifies a ten-year automatic sunset date of August 28, 2036, and termination on September 1, 2037.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes municipal policy requirements for innovation zones, including one-stop shops, expedited reviews, adaptive reuse flexibility, and sunset terms.

headings.title: Establishment of rural Missouri development fund
headings.reviewNote: Creates the rural Missouri development fund in the state treasury administered by the department.

headings.title: Definition of contributing city
headings.reviewNote: Defines contributing city as a city with a certified Missouri innovation zone that agrees to contribute a portion of net-new state sales tax revenue under section 620.6012 and ranks in the highest five percent of cities statewide by certified real property assessed valuation.

headings.title: Annual city contribution requirements and formulas
headings.reviewNote: Requires each contributing city to annually contribute ten percent of net-new state sales tax revenue retained for its innovation zone public safety fund under section 620.6012, requiring no local tax revenue.

headings.title: Eligible recipients of rural development grants
headings.reviewNote: Directs that fund moneys be awarded to rural cities, smaller non-contributing cities, or local or regional development organizations and community development corporations applying on their behalf, without requiring an innovation zone.

headings.title: Permissible uses of rural grant moneys
headings.reviewNote: Specifies permissible uses including rural education, public infrastructure or public safety, housing, workforce development or training, health care or community service facilities, and other consistent economic purposes.

headings.title: Maximum grant limitation per recipient
headings.reviewNote: Caps individual grant awards at twenty percent of total available funds in any fiscal year.

headings.title: Department grant administration and scoring criteria
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to establish competitive application procedures, scoring criteria, and annual reporting.

headings.title: Promulgation of administrative rules
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to promulgate necessary administrative rules under chapter 536 with nonseverability clauses for rules proposed or adopted after August 28, 2026.

headings.title: Severability of rural development provisions
headings.reviewNote: Provides that invalidity of any provision or application of the section shall not affect other valid provisions.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Rural Missouri Development Fund, specifying contributing city formulas, eligible rural projects, caps, and administration.

headings.title: Establishment of innovation zone public safety fund
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Missouri Innovation Zone Public Safety Fund to reinvest net-new state economic activity from certified innovation zones into public safety, public infrastructure, and related improvements.

headings.title: Fund revenue sources, separate accounting, and distribution
headings.reviewNote: Funds the account with appropriations, gifts, and fifty percent of net-new state revenue from certified zones, segregated from general revenue, accounted separately by zone and source, and distributed pro rata subject to appropriation.

headings.title: Exclusion of revenues captured by other programs
headings.reviewNote: Excludes portions of net-new state revenue already captured by super TIF, MODESA, downtown revitalization, tourism infrastructure, AIM zones, entertainment districts, or similar programs, while depositing uncaptured portions.

headings.title: Local dedicated fund account requirement
headings.reviewNote: Requires participating cities to deposit remitted moneys into a separate dedicated municipal public safety account.

headings.title: Permissible expenditures and forty percent split requirements
headings.reviewNote: Specifies eligible public safety and public realm expenditures, mandates at least forty percent each for public safety and public infrastructure, restricts police funding to sworn law enforcement, and prohibits supplanting existing funding.

headings.title: Department of revenue remittance timeline
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department of revenue to calculate and remit qualifying funds within one hundred twenty days of fiscal year close.

headings.title: Department administrative rulemaking authority
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department, consulting with the department of revenue, to promulgate implementing rules under chapter 536 with nonseverability provisions for rules proposed or adopted after August 28, 2026.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Missouri Innovation Zone Public Safety Fund, governing dedicated municipal accounts, allowable expenditures, remittances, and audits.

headings.title: Establishment of employer retention incentive
headings.reviewNote: Establishes an employer retention and reinvestment incentive within certified Missouri innovation zones.

headings.title: Definitions for retention and reinvestment program
headings.reviewNote: Defines baseline payroll, qualified company, qualified investment, retained jobs, and related statutory terms.

headings.title: Application to enter into benefit agreement
headings.reviewNote: Permits qualified companies to apply for benefit agreements providing withholding tax credits or authorized retention attributable to covered employees for tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2027.

headings.title: Notice of intent and department approval
headings.reviewNote: Sets forth notice of intent requirements and department approval procedures within forty-five calendar days.

headings.title: Withholding benefit cap, duration, and nonrefundability
headings.reviewNote: Bases withholding benefits on covered employee withholdings up to three percent of aggregate gross wages for three to ten years, nonrefundable with carryforward per agreement terms.

headings.title: Quarterly or semiannual benefit requests and verification
headings.reviewNote: Requires benefit requests and authorization on a quarterly basis (or department-authorized semiannual basis) and prohibits automatic retention or crediting without required verification.

headings.title: Exclusive use for qualifying reinvestment expenditures
headings.reviewNote: Restricts withholding benefits exclusively to qualifying reinvestment expenditures and caps total benefits at actual expenditures incurred and paid under the agreement.

headings.title: Ongoing eligibility, five-year commitment, and payroll maintenance
headings.reviewNote: Requires operating in a certified zone, committing to remain for at least five years, completing qualifying reinvestment expenditures, maintaining at least ninety-five percent of baseline payroll, and submitting requested information.

headings.title: Quarterly compliance certifications, thirty-day cure, and recapture
headings.reviewNote: Requires quarterly certifications of withholdings, payroll maintenance, and reinvestment expenditures, providing written notice and thirty calendar days to cure noncompliance before suspension, termination, and recapture.

headings.title: Ramp-up period for newly locating or expanding employers
headings.reviewNote: Permits benefit agreements for newly locating or expanding employers with baseline payroll established after a ramp-up period not exceeding four consecutive calendar quarters.

headings.title: Department audit authority and repayment or offset
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to audit qualifying reinvestment expenditures and benefit usage, requiring repayment or offset against future benefits for improperly claimed or retained amounts.

headings.title: Concurrent participation with Missouri one-start program
headings.reviewNote: Permits concurrent participation with Missouri one-start or other state programs if independently satisfied, giving priority to one-start withholding credits and prohibiting duplicate use of the same withholdings.

headings.title: Nonrefundability, five-year carryforward, and transfer ban
headings.reviewNote: Declares issued tax credits nonrefundable with up to five-year carryforward and prohibits assigning, transferring, selling, or conveying credits.

headings.title: Joint administrative rulemaking authority
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department, in coordination with the department of revenue, to promulgate implementing rules under chapter 536 with nonseverability provisions after August 28, 2026.

headings.title: Ten-year sunset and survival of prior agreements
headings.reviewNote: Sets sunset ten years after August 28, 2026 (August 28, 2036) unless reauthorized, preserving prior benefit agreements and continuing department enforcement and audit authority.

headings.title: Separate accounting from Missouri works annual caps
headings.reviewNote: Requires administering and accounting for incentives separately from section 620.2020(7) and (8) annual limitations without reducing amounts available under those subsections.

headings.title: Three-covered-employee eligibility threshold in innovation zones
headings.reviewNote: Makes qualified companies in certified innovation zones eligible with at least three covered employees notwithstanding general section 620.2020 minimum job creation requirements.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the innovation zone employer retention and reinvestment withholding benefit within Missouri Works, detailing agreements, three percent wage cap, quarterly certifications, ramp-up, concurrent One Start participation, separate caps, and ten-year sunset.

headings.title: Establishment of employer relocation incentive
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the employer relocation incentive within innovation zones in coordination with the Missouri one-start program.

headings.title: Definitions for employer relocation program
headings.reviewNote: Defines eligible relocated employee (at least seventy thousand dollars annual wages), eligible relocation expenses, eligible qualified company, primary residence, and state tax credit.

headings.title: Prohibition on duplicate retention and one-start benefits
headings.reviewNote: Bars combining section 620.6018 withholding retention or Missouri one-start reimbursement on the same payroll or relocation expenses, applying credits after section 620.809 withholding credits.

headings.title: Relocation tax credit up to five thousand dollars
headings.reviewNote: For tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2027, allows a tax credit equal to actual eligible relocation expenses paid per eligible relocated employee, up to five thousand dollars per employee per tax year.

headings.title: Application, certificate issuance, and evaluation factors
headings.reviewNote: Requires submitting an application under department rules for tax credit certificate issuance and permits considering projected net fiscal benefit, financial stability, and area economic distress.

headings.title: Nonrefundability, five-year carryforward, and transfer ban
headings.reviewNote: Declares tax credits nonrefundable with up to five-year carryforward and prohibits assigning, transferring, selling, or otherwise conveying credits.

headings.title: Recapture for failure to maintain twelve-month residence
headings.reviewNote: Subjects tax credits to recapture on the company's next tax return (or department of revenue assessment) if a relocated employee fails to maintain primary residence in Missouri for twelve consecutive months, independent of section 620.803.

headings.title: Joint administrative rulemaking authority
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department of economic development, in coordination with the department of revenue, to promulgate implementing rules under chapter 536 with nonseverability provisions after August 28, 2026.

headings.title: Ten-year sunset and continuation of prior agreements
headings.reviewNote: Sets sunset ten years after August 28, 2026 (August 28, 2036) unless reauthorized, preserving prior agreements and continuing department administration, enforcement, and audit authority.

headings.title: Separate accounting from Missouri one-start limits
headings.reviewNote: Requires administering and accounting for relocation incentives separately from Missouri one-start program limits under sections 620.800 to 620.809 without reducing funds allocable thereunder.

headings.title: Three-employee eligibility threshold in innovation zones
headings.reviewNote: Makes eligible qualified companies in certified innovation zones eligible if employing or committing within twelve months to employ at least three eligible relocated employees or new jobs.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the innovation zone employer relocation tax credit within Missouri One Start, capping credits at five thousand dollars per relocated employee, barring transfers, providing twelve-month residency recapture, and setting a ten-year sunset.

headings.title: Establishment of office-to-residential conversion incentive
headings.reviewNote: Establishes an office-to-residential conversion incentive.

headings.title: Definitions for office conversion program
headings.reviewNote: Defines qualified conversion expenditures, qualified converted building, state tax liability, substantially converted, tax credit (including chapter 144 sales/use tax eligibility when top income tax rate is 2.5% or less), taxpayer, and upper-floor housing.

headings.title: Tax credit authorization for office conversion
headings.reviewNote: For tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2027, authorizes transferable tax credits up to twenty-five percent of qualified conversion expenditures in certified innovation zones or qualifying main street districts with ten-year carryforward and pass-through allocation.

headings.title: Thirty percent credit for main street upper-floor housing
headings.reviewNote: For tax years beginning on or after January 1, 2027, authorizes transferable tax credits up to thirty percent of qualified conversion expenditures for upper-floor housing in qualified Missouri main street districts with ten-year carryforward.

headings.title: Single program, fifty million dollar cap, and reservations
headings.reviewNote: Establishes a fifty-million-dollar annual fiscal year cap across a single program, reserving fifty percent for structures over seven hundred fifty thousand gross square feet (allocable over up to ten years) and twenty-five percent for main street upper-floor housing.

headings.title: Cap exhaustion notice and waiting queue priority
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to notify awaiting applicants when annual credits are exhausted and retain applications on file in priority order for rescinded or next-fiscal-year allocations.

headings.title: Preliminary application, forty-five-day review, and documentation
headings.reviewNote: Requires preliminary applications authorized in submission order within forty-five calendar days, including proof of ownership or site control, architectural plans, cost and basis estimates, eligibility proof, and land use approvals.

headings.title: Single-property review and thirty-day cure for deficiencies
headings.reviewNote: Restricts review to the property address submitted without substitution, provides thirty days to cure incomplete applications before removal, and treats revised applications as new submissions.

headings.title: Evaluation under master scorecard
headings.reviewNote: Requires office conversion applications to be scored and ranked under the innovation zone master scorecard.

headings.title: Notice of approval or denial of tax credits
headings.reviewNote: Requires written notification of application determinations within statutory review deadlines.

headings.title: Restrictions on modifying approved taxpayer identity
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits modifying approved taxpayer identity except adding owners while retaining the same principal (or post-ten-percent principal removal for nonperformance) or ownership changes via foreclosure, deed in lieu, or bankruptcy.

headings.title: Post-approval compliance and construction milestones
headings.reviewNote: Requires submitting financing evidence within one hundred twenty days of award (thirty-day cure) and commencing conversion (incurring at least ten percent of estimated expenditures) within twelve months, with thirty-day response and ninety-day good-cause cure before rescission.

headings.title: Final application for credit certificate issuance
headings.reviewNote: Requires submitting a final application demonstrating substantial conversion, satisfactory evidence of qualified conversion expenditures, and any other reasonably requested compliance information.

headings.title: Classification as redevelopment tax credits
headings.reviewNote: Classifies office conversion tax credits as redevelopment tax credits under the tax credit accountability act.

headings.title: Disbursement schedule and credit issuance stages
headings.reviewNote: Directs issuing seventy-five percent of approved credits within forty-five calendar days and the remaining twenty-five percent within ninety calendar days of final application materials, and allows optional annual phased issuance of eighty percent prior to completion.

headings.title: Twenty-seven-year waiting period between building credits
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits issuing tax credits for qualified conversion expenditures on a qualified converted building within twenty-seven years of a previous credit issuance on that building.

headings.title: Combination with other state tax credits
headings.reviewNote: Permits authorizing and issuing conversion tax credits in addition to historic preservation tax credits under sections 253.544 to 253.559 for the same building.

headings.title: Promulgation of administrative rules
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department of economic development, in coordination with the department of revenue, to promulgate implementing rules under chapter 536 with nonseverability provisions after August 28, 2026.

headings.title: Survival of pre-expiration projects, issuances, and redemptions
headings.reviewNote: Preserves taxpayers' ability to complete projects, receive issued credits, and redeem credits authorized on or before the section's expiration date.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the office-to-residential conversion and main street upper-floor housing tax credit, detailing twenty-five and thirty percent credit tiers, fifty-million-dollar annual cap and reservations, application review, milestones, staged issuance, and survival of prior authorizations.

headings.title: Establishment of Missouri opportunity zone program
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Missouri opportunity zone program as an overlay within certified innovation zones.

headings.title: Definitions for opportunity zone investments
headings.reviewNote: Defines equity investment, inclusion event, investment property, Missouri income tax liability, Missouri opportunity zone, operating business, qualified Missouri opportunity zone fund, qualified Missouri opportunity zone investment, and taxpayer (excluding C corporations).

headings.title: Election to defer state income tax liability
headings.reviewNote: Permits taxpayers to elect to defer all or any portion of Missouri individual income tax liability invested in a qualified opportunity zone investment or fund, regardless of residency while subject to chapter 143.

headings.title: Filing procedure and verification documentation
headings.reviewNote: Requires taxpayers to elect deferral on timely filed tax returns with supporting verification forms.

headings.title: Duration of tax liability deferral
headings.reviewNote: Continues deferral until the earliest inclusion event: disposition, loss of qualification, ten years from investment, twenty-four-month operating business or thirty-month investment property failure, or annual four and seven-tenths percent net-income inclusion.

headings.title: Pro rata flow-through of fund inclusion events
headings.reviewNote: Requires inclusion events occurring in a qualified Missouri opportunity zone fund to flow through pro rata to direct and indirect taxpayers for determination, reporting, and payment of resulting tax liability.

headings.title: Independence from federal opportunity zone status
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that participation does not require federal opportunity zone certification or compliance.

headings.title: Prohibition on duplicate tax deferrals
headings.reviewNote: Prohibits deferring tax on gains that have already received another state tax deferral or exemption.

headings.title: Survival of taxpayer rights after statutory repeal
headings.reviewNote: Protects accrued tax deferral and exclusion rights of participating taxpayers if the section expires.

headings.title: Department of revenue administrative guidelines
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department of revenue to establish reporting forms and tax return reconciliation procedures.

headings.title: Annual taxpayer return reporting and CPA certification
headings.reviewNote: Requires taxpayers to report deferrals annually on Missouri income tax returns with department forms and an independent CPA investment certification, triggering immediate liability with interest and penalties upon noncompliance.

headings.title: Promulgation of administrative rules
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to promulgate rules for fund certification and the department of revenue to promulgate all other implementing rules under chapter 536 with nonseverability provisions after August 28, 2026.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Missouri Opportunity Zone overlay program allowing deferral of Missouri individual income tax liabilities reinvested in qualified zone businesses or properties, with inclusion events, flow-through recognition, and annual CPA-certified reporting.

headings.title: Establishment of angel investment incentive
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the angel investment incentive to encourage seed-stage equity investments in innovative businesses.

headings.title: Definitions for angel investment program
headings.reviewNote: Defines cash investment, qualified Missouri business, qualified security, and accredited investor.

headings.title: Authorization and calculation of tax credit
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a tax credit equal to a percentage of cash equity investments made in qualified Missouri businesses.

headings.title: Application procedure and investor certification
headings.reviewNote: Sets forth application requirements for investors and business certification with the Missouri Technology Corporation.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the angel investment tax credit incentive, defining investment terms, credit calculations, and certification procedures.

headings.title: MTC allocation and department issuance of credits
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the Missouri Technology Corporation to allocate tax credits and directs department certificate issuance.

headings.title: Immunity from liability for state and MTC
headings.reviewNote: Provides that the state, department, and MTC shall not be liable for damages or losses arising from investments.

headings.title: Transfer of unclaimed tax credits to natural persons
headings.reviewNote: Permits investors to transfer unclaimed angel investment tax credits to any natural person who may claim them against Missouri income tax liability subject to section 620.6030 limits and MTC/department transfer documentation.

headings.title: Annual reporting by qualified businesses
headings.reviewNote: Requires qualified businesses to submit annual progress reports detailing employment, wages, and capital raised.

headings.title: Exemption from personal privacy protection act
headings.reviewNote: Exempts required program disclosures from section 105.1500 of the personal privacy protection act.

headings.title: Classification under tax credit accountability act
headings.reviewNote: Classifies angel investment tax credits as entrepreneurial tax credits under section 135.800.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs MTC angel credit allocations, state liability immunity, designation loss and clawbacks, transfers to natural persons, annual and quarterly reporting, and statutory classifications.

headings.title: Development of seed capital strategy
headings.reviewNote: Requires joint development of the seed capital and commercialization strategy by economic development organizations for board approval.

headings.title: Authorization of twenty million in tax credits
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes up to twenty million dollars in aggregate tax credits for qualified funds, capped at five million annually.

headings.title: Corporation approval of professional fund managers
headings.reviewNote: Directs the corporation to approve fund managers based on federal Small Business Administration SBIC criteria.

headings.title: Department administrative rulemaking authority
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to promulgate rules to administer seed capital provisions pursuant to chapter 536.

headings.title: Corporation quarterly and contribution reporting
headings.reviewNote: Requires the corporation to report qualified contributions and verify that no single business receives over ten percent.

headings.title: Annual audited financial statements of funds
headings.reviewNote: Requires qualified funds to provide annual CPA-audited financial statements to the department within ninety days of fiscal year end.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs the Missouri seed capital and commercialization strategy, tax credit caps, manager approvals, reporting, and CPA audit requirements.

headings.title: Agreements for offering seed tax credits
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes qualified economic development organizations to contract with qualified funds allowing them to offer seed tax credits in exchange for equity.

headings.title: Mandatory revenue sharing among organizations
headings.reviewNote: Requires qualified funds to contract with organizations to share equally all equity distributions and earnings, transferring shares of dissolved entities to the corporation.

headings.title: Reinvestment of distributions in qualified funds
headings.reviewNote: Requires organizations to use fund distributions solely for reinvestment in seed, start-up, and follow-up capital for Missouri businesses.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs agreements between economic development organizations and seed funds, equity sharing requirements, and mandatory capital reinvestment.

headings.title: Exclusive investment purpose of qualified funds
headings.reviewNote: Specifies that the sole purpose of each qualified fund is making qualified business investments from qualified contributions.

headings.title: One hundred percent credit for contributions
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes a state tax credit equal to one hundred percent of qualified contributions made to qualified seed funds.

headings.title: Application for credit and ten-year carryforward
headings.reviewNote: Outlines application procedures, first-come award ordering, ten-year credit carryforward, and transferable credit provisions.

headings.title: Fifteen percent tax on uninvested capital
headings.reviewNote: Imposes a fifteen percent state tax on qualified contributions not invested in qualified businesses within required statutory timeframes.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the one-hundred-percent seed fund contribution tax credit, ten-year carryforward, and a fifteen-percent tax on uninvested capital.

headings.title: Rural regional development grants authorized
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to award rural regional development grants subject to an appropriation not exceeding five million dollars.

headings.title: Eligible groups and post-award reporting duties
headings.reviewNote: Permits grants to qualified rural regional development groups and requires tracking job creation and investment, maintaining state-certified sites, measuring workforce skills, providing an organizational chart, and documenting financial activities.

headings.title: Disqualification for out-of-state regions or large budgets
headings.reviewNote: Disqualifies any rural regional development group whose region includes a county or portion of another state or whose operating budget exceeds two hundred fifty thousand dollars.

headings.title: Application submission and planning commission review
headings.reviewNote: Requires grant applications to be submitted only by a chapter 251 or legally created regional planning commission that recognizes the group as the county economic development authority.

headings.title: Planning commission application fee authorized
headings.reviewNote: Permits regional planning commissions to charge an application fee and claim reimbursement from grant recipients for actual grant administration costs.

headings.title: Individual grant cap and geographic distribution
headings.reviewNote: Caps individual grants at one hundred fifty thousand dollars and allocates funding among the nineteen regional planning commission regions.

headings.title: Matching fund ratios based on years in operation
headings.reviewNote: Distributes grants on a three-to-one state-to-local match for groups operating two years or more and a one-to-one match for groups operating under two years, including in-kind contributions.

headings.title: Allowable uses of development grant moneys
headings.reviewNote: Lists permissible grant activities including workforce development, entrepreneurship training, regional marketing, international trade training, market and financial analysis, and demographic and market opportunity research.

headings.title: Annual reporting by grant recipients
headings.reviewNote: Requires grant recipients to submit annual reports detailing project outcomes, expenditures, and matching fund sources.

headings.title: Department administrative rulemaking authority
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to promulgate rules governing the award of grants under this section.

entries.reviewSummary: Authorizes rural regional development grants up to five million dollars annually, setting post-award duties, eligibility exclusions, planning commission submissions, matching ratios by operating history, and reporting.

headings.title: Establishment of Missouri one start program
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Missouri One Start program in the department to assist businesses with recruitment and workforce training.

headings.title: Guidelines and administrative rulemaking authority
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to publish guidelines and authorizes promulgation of rules under chapter 536.

headings.title: Online application and guidelines availability
headings.reviewNote: Requires the department to make program applications, guidelines, and materials available online.

headings.title: Contracts for marketing and advertising
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to contract with outside entities for program marketing, advertising, and promotion.

headings.title: Verification of applicant tax clearance
headings.reviewNote: Directs department verification of state tax compliance through the department of revenue prior to application approval.

headings.title: Immediate notice and forfeiture upon Chapter 7 bankruptcy
headings.reviewNote: Requires any qualified company filing Chapter 7 bankruptcy to immediately notify the department, forfeit benefits, and repay any redeemed state tax credits and retained withholding taxes.

headings.title: Repayment and clawbacks upon program default
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to require full repayment of awarded training benefits plus interest upon company default.

headings.title: Contracts for customized training services
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to contract with businesses, industries, other state agencies, and political subdivisions to implement training projects or provide recruitment services.

entries.reviewSummary: Establishes the Missouri One Start program for job recruitment and training, detailing guidelines, tax clearance, default clawbacks, and training contracts.

headings.title: Establishment of job development fund
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Missouri one start job development fund in the state treasury to hold appropriations without biennial lapse.

headings.title: Financial assistance for training projects
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to provide financial assistance for new and existing job training projects from the fund.

headings.title: Authorized uses of fund appropriations
headings.reviewNote: Directs appropriations for department-administered recruitment services and certified local education agency training projects, bars replacing striking workers, excludes purchasing equipment or facilities, and limits service-industry eligibility to interstate commerce.

headings.title: Local education agency petitions for funding
headings.reviewNote: Permits local education agencies to petition the department to utilize fund moneys for accredited vocational training programs.

headings.title: Department administrative rulemaking authority
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the department to adopt administrative rules to implement the job development fund under chapter 536.

entries.reviewSummary: Creates the Missouri One Start Job Development Fund, specifying allowable training expenditures, LEA participation, and rulemaking.

headings.title: Community college new jobs training fund
headings.reviewNote: Establishes the Missouri One Start Community College New Jobs Training Fund receiving new jobs credits through June 30, 2023, prohibiting general revenue transfers, exempting balances from lapse, and transferring unobligated funds on July 1, 2023, to the consolidated training fund.

headings.title: Community college job retention training fund
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Missouri One Start Community College Job Retention Training Fund receiving retained jobs credits through June 30, 2023, prohibiting general revenue transfers, exempting balances from lapse, and transferring unobligated funds on July 1, 2023, to the consolidated training fund.

headings.title: Consolidated community college training fund
headings.reviewNote: Creates the Missouri One Start Community College Training Fund receiving all new and retained jobs credits beginning July 1, 2023, prohibiting general revenue transfers, exempting balances from lapse, and directing timely disbursements to community college project special funds.

headings.title: Department of revenue reporting forms
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department of revenue to develop reporting forms demonstrating accurate withholding tax credits.

headings.title: Establishment of community college training projects
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes community college districts to establish training projects with department and workforce development approval.

headings.title: Proportional disbursement to project special funds
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to disburse appropriated funds to each training project special fund in proportion to remitted new or retained jobs credits, adjusting for general revenue funds disbursed upon project commencement.

headings.title: Written agreement with participating company
headings.reviewNote: Requires qualified companies to enter into formal agreements committing to job retention and training performance.

headings.title: Funding options and withholding tax credits
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes funding projects through state withholding tax credits or direct program fund appropriations.

headings.title: Issuance of training certificates by colleges
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes community college boards of trustees to issue certificates to finance current project training costs.

headings.title: Refunding certificates and sale terms
headings.reviewNote: Permits public or private sale of refunding certificates to refinance outstanding training obligations.

headings.title: Public notice of intent to issue certificates
headings.reviewNote: Requires published public notice before community college boards of trustees issue financing certificates.

headings.title: Board findings regarding company financial capacity
headings.reviewNote: Requires board findings confirming the qualified company possesses the financial capacity to meet obligations.

headings.title: Certificates not deemed state indebtedness
headings.reviewNote: Clarifies that certificates issued by community colleges do not constitute general indebtedness of the state.

headings.title: Sunset provisions under Missouri sunset act
headings.reviewNote: Reauthorizes sections 620.800 to 620.809 as of August 28, 2018, sets expiration on August 28, 2030 (twelve years if reauthorized), and sets termination on September 1 of the following calendar year (September 1, 2031).

headings.title: Preservation of prior program agreements
headings.reviewNote: Preserves the validity and terms of any department agreement or obligation made under sections 620.800 to 620.809 prior to August 28, 2019.

entries.reviewSummary: Governs Missouri One Start community college training funds, certificate financing, withholding credits, trustee duties, and sunset terms.

headings.title: Citation of Citizen's Land Development Cooperative Act
headings.reviewNote: Designates the statutory section as the Citizen's Land Development Cooperative Act.

headings.title: Definitions for land development cooperatives
headings.reviewNote: Defines citizen's land development cooperative, commission, and department.

headings.title: Establishment of cooperative commission
headings.reviewNote: Creates the citizen's land development cooperative commission within the department and outlines member composition.

headings.title: Quorum and commission organizational meetings
headings.reviewNote: Authorizes the commission to conduct business upon quorum and adopt internal bylaws and operating procedures.

headings.title: Information gathering and annual reporting
headings.reviewNote: Directs the commission to gather information, recommend cooperative policies, local referenda guidelines, and tax reforms, and report annually to the governor and general assembly.

headings.title: Grant program and cooperative fund created
headings.reviewNote: Creates the citizen's land development cooperative fund to provide startup grants and loans to local communities.

headings.title: Department administrative rulemaking authority
headings.reviewNote: Directs the department to establish implementing rules under chapter 536 with nonseverability clauses for rules proposed or adopted after August 28, 2022.

entries.reviewSummary: Enacts the Citizen's Land Development Cooperative Act, establishing the commission, reporting duties, trust fund, and grants.
